findings.text: The allocation info file exposes open read positioning release and control operations through a single operations table where open reserves per file private state and prepares its control synchronization while release tears that synchronization down and frees the state.

Per file private state keeps a current iterator plus a last reported iterator plus a separate control iterator together with a header flag a filter value a positioned flag and a control mutex so that sequential reads and control queries do not disturb each other.

Sequential reading starts by guarding the module list and either starting a fresh scan with header output at the beginning or resuming from the last reported position elsewhere then each step remembers the current entry advances the scan and counts position while display writes the header once followed by one entry line and termination releases the module guard.
The human readable report begins with a version marker indicating major version two minor version zero followed by a column legend describing size calls and tag information.
Each entry line conveys live byte usage and call count together with tag identity and appends an inaccurate marker when the underlying counters are flagged as approximate.

Long names are reduced to a trailing suffix that fits the fixed field capacity reserving room for termination while copy stores padded fixed size form and comparison operates on the same truncated representation.

Conversion from internal tag to control output copies module function and file names plus line number and live byte and call totals and derives an accuracy flag as the negation of the internal inaccurate state with empty module name when none is present.

Control handling supports queries for content identity retrieval by filtered position and retrieval of the following filtered entry with unknown commands rejected with ENOIOCTLCMD and compatibility handling translating the user pointer before delegating to the common path.

Filtering accepts every entry when no mask is set otherwise each requested attribute must match including module function file and line equality inaccurate state equality and byte total within optional minimum and maximum bounds with live counters fetched only when a size bound is present and a missing module name matching only an empty request.

Positional retrieval validates user memory access and mask bits and size bound ordering and range against the current entry count reporting EFAULT EINVAL or ENOENT without changing iterator state on rejection.

Positional retrieval stores the supplied filter or clears it when absent then scans from the start skipping matching entries until the requested offset is reached and marks the handle positioned on success while next retrieval initializes the scan when unpositioned then returns the next match or clears the positioned mark when exhausted.

Control queries serialize per handle iterator filter and positioned state with the private mutex while also holding the global module list guard during count reads and scans with the private guard acquired first and both guards released before results are copied back to user space.

Sequential iteration holds the global module list guard from start until stop while ranking of heavy users takes the same guard in blocking form when sleeping is allowed and in try form otherwise returning no results when the try fails.

A ranking helper returns up to a caller supplied number of highest byte consumers in descending order using ordered insertion with shifting and reports zero entries when the tag registry is unavailable.
Splitting a compound page does nothing when profiling is inactive or the original page carries no tag otherwise every resulting sub range beyond the first inherits a reference to the original tag.

Exchanging tags between two pages does nothing when profiling is inactive or either page lacks a tag or references cannot be acquired otherwise both references are emptied before the tags are exchanged and the handles are released.

Compressed mode initialization resolves the kernel tag section bounds by name derives the entry count and verifies that the count fits the available page flag capacity disabling profiling when oversized and otherwise publishing a bit offset and mask while shutdown disables profiling optionally removes the info file and records support as unavailable.

Kernel tag anchoring uses a first pointer plus count pair with global reference mask and offset values while module handling uses a range allocation tree plus a virtual mapping pointer plus placeholder module objects and a module section descriptor.

Size handling leaves values unchanged when compression is inactive otherwise values are rounded up to tag multiples prepend amounts are similarly aligned only when tag size meets required alignment addressability requires the combined identifier space to fit the flag capacity section memory is needed only with support and at least tag sized requests and cleanup frees per cpu counters whose byte total is zero reporting whether all were empty.

Per cpu deallocation ignores null pointers otherwise it translates to a chunk address locates the owning chunk frees the area under guard warns once on invalid frees invokes tag and accounting hooks evaluates full chunk and reclaim conditions emits a trace record and schedules balancing work when required.
Per cpu deallocation holds the global per cpu guard with interrupt state preserved across area release hook invocation and reclaim evaluation releasing before any scheduling of background balancing.

Per cpu leak tracking removal is gated on tracking being enabled and the pointer being present and valid then a full deletion looks up and detaches the record and finalizes it while a missing record is silently ignored to tolerate unmatched frees.

Leak record lookup and detachment execute under the global leak guard with interrupt state preserved while final deletion clears the allocated state under the per record guard with interrupt state preserved before dropping the reference.

Record search selects a tree by physical versus per cpu versus ordinary kind strips address tags then walks by interval ordering returning on exact match or any containing interval when aliasing is allowed and otherwise emitting a deferred alias warning with record details before reporting absence.

Tree selection prefers the physical root when flagged then the per cpu root when flagged and otherwise the ordinary root while type labeling yields a physical suffix a per cpu suffix or an empty label in the same priority.

Detachment erases the record from its tree conditionally unlinks it from the global list and marks it removed while deletion asserts allocated state and live references clears the allocated mark and drops a reference and the final drop frees directly when no cache exists and otherwise defers freeing through the reclamation callback.
Record diagnosis reports address size creator identity timing and counters plus flags checksum and a stack trace when present aiding alias and leak investigation.
Content identity retrieval guards the module list while sampling the current identifier releases the guard and then copies the single value to user space reporting EFAULT when that copy fails.
